questions.prompt: A box holds years 1 through 100. Where does year 101 go?
questions.explanation: The first box is full at year 100. Year 101 starts the second group of one hundred years.

questions.prompt: The 19th century runs from 1801 to 1900. Which century contains 1900?
questions.explanation: 1900 is the last year of the 19th century. The next century starts in 1901.
The 20th century ended in 2000. The next year, 2001, began the 21st.

title: What century is 1900? The dates that trip us up

sources.name: US Naval Observatory — The 21st century and 3rd millennium

practice: Try History Quiz and see which periods you recognise.

sections.title: Is 1900 in the 19th or 20th century?
sections.html:
1900 is the last year of the 19th century. The 20th century begins in 1901 and ends in 2000. Those first two digits are a tempting shortcut, but they miss the boundary.

As the US Naval Observatory explains, the Common Era starts with year 1, not year 0.

sections.title: Imagine boxes holding 100 year cards
sections.html:
Box one holds years 1–100. Card 100 fills its last space, so 101 starts box two. Keep going and each numbered box is one century.

The same rule puts 1900 at the end of the nineteenth box. The next card, 1901, starts the twentieth.

sections.title: 19th, 20th and 21st century dates
sections.html:
First and last years, using CE/AD numbering
CenturyYears
19th1801–1900
20th1901–2000
21st2001–2100

So the 21st century began in 2001, even though the change to a year beginning with “20” happened in 2000.

sections.title: Is “the 1900s” the same as the 20th century?
sections.html:
When it means the hundred-year range 1900–1999, no: that range starts and ends a year earlier than the 20th century, 1901–2000. The wording matters.

These examples use CE/AD dates. For another way old dates can look unfamiliar, try reading Roman numerals in small chunks.

description: 1900 belongs to the 19th century; 1901 starts the 20th. Compare the 19th, 20th and 21st centuries, and see why “the 1900s” is a different range.
